nodes.content: Design an incremental change-impact analyzer that safely minimizes regression tests despite dynamic dispatch, reflection, and generated code.
requirements: Never exclude potentially affected tests when reflection, generated code, or missing dependencies prevent definitive analysis.
Match full-suite failure detection while selecting at most 40% of tests across 100 benchmark revisions.

nodes.content: Build TraceGuard: combine incremental call graphs, dispatch traces, reflection instrumentation, and generated-source provenance; run the full suite for unresolved edges.
Can TraceGuard's full-suite fallback for unresolved edges remain rare enough to meet the 40% selection cap across 100 revisions?
TraceGuard will need full-suite fallback in at most five revisions and select at most 35% otherwise, averaging at most 38.25%.
Benchmark TraceGuard on 100 revisions, recording fallback frequency, mean selected-test fraction, and failure recall against full-suite baselines.
Run TraceGuard and full suites on RevisionBench-100; record unresolved-edge fallbacks, per-revision selection rates, and missed failures.
RevisionBench-100 had four full-suite fallbacks; remaining revisions selected at most 34%, averaging 27% overall with zero missed failures.
Adopt TraceGuard with conservative full-suite fallback: RevisionBench-100 averaged 27% selected tests and detected every full-suite failure.
Deploy TraceGuard in CI; trace dispatch/reflection, track generated-source provenance, and run full suites for unresolved or missing dependencies.
TraceGuard CI integration includes conservative dependency analysis, full-suite fallback for unresolved edges, and RevisionBench-100 selection and failure-detection reports.
Derive UncertaintyBench-40 from RevisionBench-100 with ambiguous dispatch, reflection, generated-code, and missing-JAR faults; compare TraceGuard selections against full suites.
On UncertaintyBench-40, reflective calls bypassed TraceGuard's fallback, omitting three tests that failed under full-suite runs.
Replay UncertaintyBench-40 with instrumented MethodHandles, Method.invoke, and ServiceLoader; compare TraceGuard selections against full-suite failures by reflective entry point.
Instrumented MethodHandles exposed unresolved targets and triggered full-suite fallback; the replay detected all three previously missed failures.
Will unresolved MethodHandles targets raise full-suite fallback above five revisions or mean test selection above 40% on RevisionBench-100?
Rerun RevisionBench-100 with MethodHandles instrumentation and conservative unresolved-target fallback; measure fallback revisions, mean selection, and full-suite failure recall.
Execute the instrumented RevisionBench-100 rerun; count unresolved-target fallbacks and compare selected tests and detected failures with full suites.
RevisionBench-100 rerun report contains per-revision fallback causes, selected-test fractions, and full-suite failure comparisons.
Certify exclusions using dependency proofs; include tests in unresolved dispatch, reflection, generated-code, and missing-dependency cones; full-suite fallback if unbounded.
Can dependency proofs bound MethodHandles and generated-source uncertainty cones without excluding affected tests or exceeding 40% mean selection?
Proof-bounded uncertainty cones with unbounded-edge fallback will retain every affected test and average ≤40% selection on RevisionBench-100.
Run proof-bounded cones on RevisionBench-100; audit excluded tests against full suites and measure mean selection and fallback frequency.
On RevisionBench-100, proof-bounded cones selected 44% of tests on average, with zero missed failures; generated-code fallbacks drove excess.
Extend proof-bounded cones with hermetic generator-input fingerprints and generated-source provenance; use full suites when inputs or provenance are unresolved.
Rerun RevisionBench-100 with generator-input fingerprints and provenance manifests; audit fallback triggers, excluded tests, mean selection, and full-suite failures.
RevisionBench-100 averaged 36% test selection with zero missed failures; seven revisions with unresolved generator inputs ran full suites.
Mutate generator inputs, provenance manifests, MethodHandles targets, and missing JARs in UncertaintyBench-40; audit exclusions against full-suite failures.
On UncertaintyBench-40, symlinked generator templates escaped input fingerprints, falsely certifying provenance and excluding two tests that failed in full suites.
Can canonicalized symlink targets enter generator fingerprints without pushing RevisionBench-100 selection above 40% or missing affected tests?
Canonicalizing symlink targets before fingerprinting, with fallback for unresolved paths, will restore zero missed failures at ≤40% mean selection.
Canonicalize generator-input symlinks, fall back on unresolved paths, then rerun UncertaintyBench-40 and RevisionBench-100 against full suites.
Implement realpath-based generator-input fingerprints with unresolved-path fallback; rerun both benchmarks, auditing missed failures and RevisionBench-100 mean selection.
Realpath fingerprints selected both previously missed UncertaintyBench-40 tests; both benchmarks had zero missed failures, and RevisionBench-100 averaged 38%.
Inject dangling and cyclic symlinks into generator inputs; verify full-suite fallback, then recalculate RevisionBench-100 mean selection and failure recall.
Dangling and cyclic symlinks triggered full-suite fallback with zero missed failures, but RevisionBench-100 mean selection rose from 38% to 42%.
Can hermetic generator traces prove dangling or cyclic symlinks unused, reducing 42% mean selection below 40% without unsafe exclusions?
Complete hermetic generator filesystem traces will certify unaccessed broken symlinks, lowering RevisionBench-100 mean selection below 40% without missed failures.
Retain realpath fingerprints and broken-symlink fallback; certify unused links via complete hermetic traces, then rerun both benchmarks against full suites.
Sandbox generator filesystem access; certify unused broken links only with complete traces; measure selection and failure recall on both benchmarks.
Complete sandbox traces certified unused broken symlinks; RevisionBench-100 averaged 39% selection, and both benchmarks matched full-suite failures.
Adopt realpath fingerprints and complete sandbox traces; retain full-suite fallback for unresolved inputs: 39% mean selection, zero missed failures.
Integrate adopted generator tracing into CI; retain full-suite fallback for incomplete traces and verify 39% mean selection and failure parity.
CI patch adds realpath generator fingerprints, sandbox trace completeness checks, and full-suite fallback for unresolved inputs.
Use SoundSlice: classloader-backed per-test reachability certificates with dispatch closure; unresolved reflection, generators, or missing dependencies trigger full-suite fallback.
Can SoundSlice invalidate per-test certificates when classloaders dynamically introduce implementations, without exceeding 40% mean selection on RevisionBench-100?
Fingerprinting classloader hierarchies and loaded implementation sets will invalidate stale certificates, preserving failure recall at ≤40% mean selection.
Replay RevisionBench-100 with dynamically injected implementations; compare certificate invalidation, mean selection, and failure recall against full suites.
RevisionBench-100 invalidated 12 stale certificates; SoundSlice averaged 37% selection and detected every full-suite failure.
Replay SoundSlice on RevisionBench-100; compare per-revision fallbacks, selection rates, and failure detection against the instrumented TraceGuard report.
On RevisionBench-100, post-certificate generator reruns caused SoundSlice to omit two full-suite-failing tests that instrumented TraceGuard selected.
Instrument generator reruns between certificate issuance and test execution; audit SoundSlice invalidation against full-suite failures on RevisionBench-100.
Generator-rerun instrumentation invalidated both stale certificates before execution; SoundSlice selected both previously omitted failing tests on RevisionBench-100.
Does generator-rerun invalidation retain SoundSlice's ≤40% mean selection while preventing stale certificates from excluding affected tests?
Using observed generator-rerun failures and invalidation instrumentation, rerun RevisionBench-100; audit certificate exclusions, mean selection, and full-suite failure parity.
Run generator-rerun-aware SoundSlice on RevisionBench-100; compare certificate invalidations, mean selection, and detected failures against full suites.
Generator-rerun-aware SoundSlice invalidated 14 certificates on RevisionBench-100, averaged 39% selection, and matched every full-suite failure.
Adopt SoundSlice only with pre-execution generator-rerun invalidation: it fixed earlier omissions and matched full-suite failures at 39% mean selection.
Gate CI test selection on fresh SoundSlice certificates after generator reruns; audit fallback reasons, selection percentage, and full-suite failure parity.
SoundSlice CI gate verifies certificate freshness after generator reruns, falls back for unresolved dependencies, and logs selection and failure-parity metrics.
ModuleFence proves module isolation, selects every test in uncertain modules, and runs full suites when boundaries remain unproven.
Can ModuleFence prove isolation across reflective service loading and generated adapters while keeping RevisionBench-100 mean selection at most 40%?
ModuleFence's service-provider registry and generated-adapter manifests will certify module boundaries, preserving all failures at ≤40% mean selection.
Catalog service-provider registries and generated-adapter manifests, then benchmark ModuleFence against full suites for selection rate and failure recall.
Benchmark ModuleFence against realpath-trace and SoundSlice CI gates on RevisionBench-100; audit service/adapter boundaries, mean selection, and missed failures.
RevisionBench-100 showed ModuleFence at 35% mean selection with zero missed failures; realpath-trace and SoundSlice each averaged 39%.
Inject runtime ServiceLoader providers and regenerated adapters into UncertaintyBench-40; audit ModuleFence exclusions against full-suite failures.
UncertaintyBench-40 exposed a runtime ServiceLoader provider outside ModuleFence's registry; its module was excluded despite one full-suite-failing test.
Can ModuleFence detect runtime ServiceLoader provider additions before selection without exceeding 40% mean selection on RevisionBench-100?
Hashing runtime provider inventories before selection and invalidating changed boundaries will restore failure parity at ≤40% mean selection.
Starting from 35% selection and the missed runtime provider, hash provider inventories before selection; rerun both benchmarks against full suites.
Implement preselection ServiceLoader inventory hashes; invalidate changed ModuleFence boundaries and compare both benchmarks' selections and failures with full suites.
Provider-inventory hashes selected the previously omitted failing test; ModuleFence averaged 38% on RevisionBench-100 with zero missed failures across both benchmarks.
Inject ServiceLoader providers after inventory hashing but before test selection; audit ModuleFence omissions and RevisionBench-100 selection against full suites.
Post-hash provider injection escaped ModuleFence invalidation, excluding one full-suite-failing test despite 38% mean selection.
Can classloader load hooks invalidate ModuleFence's provider snapshot through test execution without raising RevisionBench-100 mean selection above 40%?
Classloader hooks plus atomic provider snapshots will rerun selection on late additions, preserving failure parity at ≤40% mean selection.
Build on 38% preselection hashing and the post-hash miss: hook provider loads, invalidate snapshots atomically, then rerun both benchmarks.
Instrument classloader provider loads and atomic snapshot invalidation; replay late-injection cases and RevisionBench-100 against full suites.
Classloader hooks caught the late provider, selected its failing test, and yielded 39% mean selection with zero missed RevisionBench-100 failures.
Adopt ModuleFence with atomic snapshots, classloader hooks, and unresolved-provider fallback; earlier misses were fixed at 39% mean selection.
Deploy ModuleFence CI gate with atomic provider snapshots, classloader hooks, reselection on late loads, and full-suite uncertainty fallback.
ModuleFence CI gate records provider snapshot versions, classloader invalidations, conservative fallback decisions, and RevisionBench-100 failure-parity metrics.
